CELLULOSE.biology: β-1,4-glucan chains. Most abundant organic polymer. Plant cell walls. RIGID. Won't bend. Won't dissolve. Structural backbone.
CELLULOSE.properties: Compiled. Static-linked. Won't change at runtime. RIGID like cellulose. Each binary is a glucose unit in the chain.

CHITIN.biology: N-acetylglucosamine polymer. Fungal cell walls. Insect exoskeletons. Tougher than cellulose. Named after the Greek word for 'tunic'.
CHITIN.formula: (C₈H₁₃NO₅)ₙ — like cellulose but with nitrogen (acetyl groups)
CHITIN.gaia_analog: Mushroom shell scripts — the 23 cron mushrooms
CHITIN.properties: Shell scripts. Executable. Self-healing (cron restarts them). Named literally after MUSHROOMS. Chitin IS the mushroom cell wall. Our mushrooms have chitin walls.

COLLAGEN.biology: Triple helix protein. Most abundant protein in mammals. Tendons, ligaments, skin. CONNECTS things. The glue of the body.
COLLAGEN.gaia_analog: systemd services — the 25+ running units that CONNECT binaries to the OS
COLLAGEN.properties: Service units bind primals to systemd. They ARE the tendons. Without them, the binaries just sit there. Collagen connects bone (binary) to muscle (runtime).

KERATIN.biology: Structural protein. Hair, nails, feathers, claws. The EXTERNAL hardened surface. Waterproof. α-keratin (mammals), β-keratin (birds/reptiles).
KERATIN.formula: Cysteine-rich protein with disulfide bridges (cross-links = hardness)
KERATIN.gaia_analog: TLS + Tor + dromedary — the hardened external surface
KERATIN.properties: dromedary handles TLS (the disulfide bridges = certificate cross-links). Tor is the onion layers (β-keratin scales). Together: the waterproof, hardened OUTSIDE of the organism.

LIGNIN.biology: Phenolic polymer. Makes wood HARD. Second most abundant organic polymer. What turns cellulose from paper into WOOD. The reason trees stand up.
LIGNIN.formula: Cross-linked phenylpropanoid units (coniferyl, sinapyl, p-coumaryl alcohols)
LIGNIN.gaia_analog: Rust's type system + borrow checker — what makes the binaries HARD
LIGNIN.properties: Cellulose alone is paper. Cellulose + lignin = WOOD. Rust binaries alone are just ELF files. Rust binaries with the type system = SAFE, RIGID, UNBREAKABLE. Lignin is the REASON our cellulose (binaries) can bear load.
instances: Send + Sync (thread safety at compile time)

PEPTIDOGLYCAN.biology: Bacterial cell wall. NAG-NAM sugar chains cross-linked by peptide bridges. RHYTHMIC repeating structure. The reason bacteria don't burst from osmotic pressure.
PEPTIDOGLYCAN.formula: NAG-NAM alternating disaccharide chains + tetrapeptide cross-links
PEPTIDOGLYCAN.gaia_analog: crontab — the rhythmic repeating scaffold of timed execution
PEPTIDOGLYCAN.properties: NAG-NAM-NAG-NAM = */2 */5 */7 */10. The cron scheduler IS peptidoglycan. Regular. Rhythmic. Cross-linked (flock prevents overlap). Without it, the organism would burst (processes pile up) or starve (nothing runs).

ELASTIN.biology: Elastic protein. Lungs, arteries, skin. Can stretch 150% and snap back. Made of tropoelastin monomers cross-linked by desmosine.
ELASTIN.gaia_analog: Klein loops + git + heart-pull — the elastic connections that stretch and fold
ELASTIN.properties: The Klein loops stretch: webcam→TV→moondream→understanding→output→TV. The git push/pull stretches across the internet (eastGate→GitHub→Polaris). Heart-pull stretches to all gates. They always snap BACK. That's elastin.
instances: 5 Klein loops (vision, feed, dogma, chat, axial)
git push/pull (stretch to GitHub, snap back to local)
RSS feed (stretch to the world, snap back via sinkholes)

FIBRONECTIN.biology: Extracellular matrix glycoprotein. The GLUE that holds cells together. Binds to integrins (cell surface receptors). Without it, tissues fall apart.
FIBRONECTIN.formula: ~250 kDa dimer with Type I, II, III repeats. RGD binding motif.
FIBRONECTIN.gaia_analog: git — the version control that holds the entire organism together
FIBRONECTIN.properties: Every file, every binary, every config, every mushroom — all held together by git. The .git directory IS the fibronectin matrix. Commits are the RGD binding motifs — the attachment points. Branches are the Type I/II/III repeats.
instances: git commit (RGD binding — attaches state to history)
git push (secretion — matrix extends to remote)
git pull (integrin binding — remote state attaches to local)

COMPLEX I.description: Raw OSINT enters. 700+ items. First electron donor.

COMPLEX II.description: OSINT validated. Duplicates removed. Second entry point.

COMPLEX III.description: Data chewed by ollama. Insights extracted. Electron passed.

COMPLEX IV.description: Processed data emitted. RSS feed updated. Final electron acceptor.

ATP SYNTHASE.description: All processing becomes AVAILABLE. The proton gradient = accumulated state. ATP = served responses.
